subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which two pieces are the Edexcel set works for the 'Instrumental music 1700-1820' area of study?
options: Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 (3rd movement) and Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 8 'Pathetique' (1st movement)
Bach's 'Air on the G String' and Beethoven's Symphony No. 5
questions.explain: The two prescribed instrumental set works are Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 third movement and the first movement of Beethoven's 'Pathetique' Sonata.

questions.q: In which key is Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 8 'Pathetique'?
questions.explain: The 'Pathetique' Sonata (Op. 13) is written in the dramatic key of C minor.

questions.q: Which three instruments make up the concertino (solo group) in Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5?
questions.explain: The concertino comprises solo flute, violin and harpsichord, with the harpsichord given an unusually prominent role.

questions.q: What does the term 'concerto grosso' describe?
options: Contrast between a small group of soloists (concertino) and the full ensemble (ripieno)
A solo concerto for a single virtuoso performer
A large symphony in four movements
A piece built entirely on a repeating bass line
questions.explain: A concerto grosso sets a small solo group (concertino) against the larger accompanying body (ripieno/tutti).

questions.q: The first movement of the 'Pathetique' Sonata opens with a slow, solemn introduction. Which tempo/expression marking indicates this?
questions.explain: The movement begins Grave, meaning slow and solemn, before the fast Allegro di molto e con brio.

questions.q: A student hears a Baroque orchestral movement in which a recurring tutti theme keeps returning between contrasting passages for the soloists. Which structural device is being used?
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a returning tutti refrain (the ritornello) with episodes for the soloists, typical of the Baroque concerto.

questions.q: Which textural feature is most characteristic of the third movement of Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5?
questions.explain: The lively finale opens fugally, with the parts entering in imitation to create contrapuntal texture.

questions.q: Who composed the song 'Music for a While'?
questions.explain: 'Music for a While' is a Baroque song by the English composer Henry Purcell.

questions.q: 'Music for a While' is built over a short, repeating bass line. What is this device called?
questions.explain: The song is constructed over a ground bass, a repeated bass pattern that underpins the whole piece.

questions.q: In 'Music for a While', the word 'eternal' is set to a long, elaborate run of notes on a single syllable. What is this technique called?
questions.explain: Purcell uses a melisma, many notes to one syllable, to word-paint the sense of something everlasting.

questions.q: A singer performs repeated, detached notes on the word 'drop' so the music seems to fall like drops. Which compositional technique does this illustrate?
questions.explain: Matching the music to the meaning of the text, as on 'drop', is known as word painting (text painting).

questions.q: Which member of Queen wrote the song 'Killer Queen'?
questions.explain: 'Killer Queen', from the album Sheer Heart Attack, was written by Freddie Mercury.

questions.q: Which vocal feature is a hallmark of Queen's sound in 'Killer Queen'?
questions.explain: Queen layered multi-tracked, close-harmony vocals in the studio to create their rich choral backing texture.

questions.q: 'Defying Gravity' is a song from which stage musical?
questions.explain: 'Defying Gravity', by Stephen Schwartz, is the Act 1 finale of the musical Wicked.

questions.q: In 'Defying Gravity', the music shifts up into a new key to heighten the emotional climax. What is this device called?
questions.explain: Schwartz uses modulation, moving to a higher key, to intensify the drama at the song's climax.

questions.q: In film music, a short recurring musical idea associated with a particular character or theme is known as a:
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme linked to a character, place or idea, a technique central to the Star Wars score.

questions.q: Who composed the music for the Star Wars set work studied in this component?
questions.explain: The Star Wars score, including the 'Main Title', was composed by John Williams.

questions.q: A film cue opens with a bold brass fanfare over a full orchestral tutti to signal an epic, heroic adventure. Which set-work opening best matches this description?
questions.explain: The Star Wars 'Main Title' opens with a triumphant brass fanfare and full orchestra to establish its heroic character.

questions.q: The set work 'Release' is performed by which act?
questions.explain: 'Release' is by Afro Celt Sound System, from their album Volume 2: Release.

questions.q: Which combination of styles does Afro Celt Sound System's 'Release' fuse together?
options: African, Celtic and electronic dance music
questions.explain: 'Release' blends West African and Celtic (Irish) traditions with electronic dance music and studio production.

questions.q: You hear a track led by a virtuosic jazz double bass and voice, layered over a gently swaying Brazilian samba/bossa nova rhythm. Which fusion set work is this?
questions.explain: Esperanza Spalding's 'Samba Em Prelude' fuses jazz (featuring her double bass and vocals) with Brazilian samba and bossa nova.
